note: Token Views Filter adds a 'Use tokens' checkbox (option use_tokens) to core Views filters (ids string/numeric/date/datetime/combine/list_field/geofield_proximity_filter) by class-swapping same-id plugins via hook_views_plugins_filter_alter(). The real persisted state is use_tokens: true plus a tokenised value on a filter handler inside a views.view.* config entity; TokensFilterTrait::preQuery() resolves the token with the core token service. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that config: introspection reads a known tvf_* View's tokenised filter, execution enables use_tokens and sets a token value, verified against the live View config. All fixtures are namespaced View config entities prefixed tvf_ and deleted on cleanup.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal token_views_filter module let you do in a View, and which UI control turns it on for a filter?
evals.expected_output: It lets a Views filter's value contain replacement tokens (e.g. [current-user:uid]). You enable it by ticking the 'Use tokens' checkbox on a string/numeric/date/datetime/combine/list_field/geofield_proximity filter's settings; it stores use_tokens: true on that filter.

evals.prompt: With token_views_filter, where is the 'use tokens' setting saved for a Views filter, and how is the token in the value actually resolved at runtime?
evals.expected_output: It is stored as use_tokens: true on the filter handler inside the View config entity (views.view.<id>). At query time TokensFilterTrait::preQuery() calls the core token service: token->replace($value, ['view'=>$view], ['clear'=>TRUE]) against the view/current-page token types.

evals.prompt: Using token_views_filter, how would I make a content View show only nodes authored by the currently logged-in user, without a contextual filter? Give an example token.
evals.expected_output: Add an author/uid filter, tick 'Use tokens', and set its value to [current-user:uid]. token_views_filter replaces the token at query time so the View is scoped to the viewer.

evals.prompt: This site has a View with machine name 'tvf_known' that uses token_views_filter on one of its filters. Inspect the live View configuration and report the token value configured on that tokenised filter.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.tvf_known the 'title' filter has use_tokens: true and value '[current-user:uid]'. Read with: drush cget views.view.tvf_known display.default.display_options.filters.title.

evals.prompt: The View 'tvf_toggle' on this site has two filters, 'title' and 'created'. Exactly one has token replacement enabled via token_views_filter. Inspect the live View config and state which filter has 'use tokens' enabled.
evals.expected_output: The 'title' filter has use_tokens: true in views.view.tvf_toggle; the other filter does not. Check display.default.display_options.filters.*.use_tokens.

evals.prompt: This site has a View 'tvf_task' with a 'title' string filter that currently does NOT use tokens. Using token_views_filter, enable token replacement on that filter and set its value to [current-user:uid]. Apply the change to the live View.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.tvf_task the title filter must have use_tokens: true and value '[current-user:uid]'. E.g. drush cset -y views.view.tvf_task display.default.display_options.filters.title.use_tokens true and set the value to [current-user:uid].

evals.prompt: The View 'tvf_build' on this site has a 'title' string filter without token support. Make that filter's value resolve to the site name using token_views_filter (token [site:name]) and apply it to the live View.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.tvf_build the title filter must have use_tokens: true and value '[site:name]'.
